reference: Installed zstd CLI; independent raw-block frames encoded from the Zstandard frame format and small frames generated by the installed encoder. Contract cases state preservation/override requirements independently.
coverage: Validate no-operand encoding and decoding, empty encoding, and levels 1/19 by decoding every produced frame with the independent installed CLI. Encoded files are removed because valid encoder byte layouts differ; all decoded bytes and remaining files are compared.
The installed encoder creates small ordinary frames with and without a content size; decode from files and a finite pipe, keeping binary output exact.
Unlike zstdcat, zstd -dc rejects ordinary uncompressed input; do not widen strict decoding while fixing the alias.
Force enables pass-through with explicit -c and with implicit stdin stdout. Copy binary bytes without interpreting a later embedded frame magic.
Installed CLI option order selects named output for -c -o and stdout for -o -c. Decode a complete independent frame so this checks publication and output selection.
Successful named decode preserves source mode/mtime and --rm removes the source only after completion. Check timestamps explicitly because the harness compares bytes, modes and links.
Refuse an existing named target without force; retain both original input and destination.
Independent preservation contract: direct source, hardlink source alias and symlink destination must be refused under force, leaving bytes and link topology intact.

Independent atomic-publication contract (stronger than CLI parity): a recognized but truncated frame must fail with --rm and force, preserving the previous destination and source and cleaning temporary files.

Documented override contract: an unavailable relative library fails without affecting the shell; unset and empty overrides use the linked decoder successfully. Fresh process avoids caching a prior library.
Decode supported empty, skippable, unknown-size and ordinary frames in a single bounded stream.
A missing operand and a recognized incomplete frame both fail; continue to decode the subsequent valid input, returning aggregate failure.

Restored all original encoding, binary/empty stdin, named multi-input, source retention/removal, force/no-clobber, option-gap and unavailable encoder-library cases; independent CLI decoding checks format interoperability.
--no-content-size acceptance, independent frame-header flag inspection and decoded bytes for named, stdin and empty inputs.
exclusions: Full zstd CLI conformance is not claimed: other formats, legacy frames, dictionaries, decoder windows above 128 MiB and options beyond the explicitly compared subset remain unqualified. --no-content-size is explicitly compared.
Encoder bytes differ from the CLI; interoperability checks compare decoded bytes.
No large allocations, stress/crash cases, terminal interaction, injected I/O failures or dynamic override library ABI fixtures.

The compared subset places options before file operands. GNU option permutation after operands remains unqualified; the first private header-check fixture attempt used that unsupported ordering and is retained as evidence.

cases.purpose: Validate no-operand encoding and decoding, empty encoding, and levels 1/19 by decoding every produced frame with the independent installed CLI. Encoded files are removed because valid encoder byte layouts differ; all decoded bytes and remaining files are compared.
cases.script:
printf 'ordinary input\n' > plain
: > empty
for args in '' '-1' '-19'; do
 zstd -q $args < plain > encoded
 /usr/bin/zstd -qdc encoded > decoded
 /usr/bin/cmp plain decoded
 rm encoded
done
zstd -q < empty > encoded
/usr/bin/zstd -qdc encoded > empty.back
rm encoded
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > input.zst
zstd -qdc < input.zst

cases.purpose: The installed encoder creates small ordinary frames with and without a content size; decode from files and a finite pipe, keeping binary output exact.
cases.script:
printf '%b' 'binary\x00payload\xff\n' > plain
/usr/bin/zstd -q -c plain > sized.zst
/usr/bin/zstd -q --no-content-size -c plain > stream.zst
zstd -dc sized.zst
cat stream.zst | zstd -dc -

cases.purpose: Unlike zstdcat, zstd -dc rejects ordinary uncompressed input; do not widen strict decoding while fixing the alias.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x70\x6c\x61\x69\x6e\x00\x62\x79\x74\x65\x73\xff\x0a' > plain
zstd -dc plain

cases.purpose: Force enables pass-through with explicit -c and with implicit stdin stdout. Copy binary bytes without interpreting a later embedded frame magic.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x72\x61\x77\x00\xff\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > plain
zstd -dfc plain
zstd -df < plain
zstd -df - < plain
cat plain | zstd -dfc

cases.purpose: Installed CLI option order selects named output for -c -o and stdout for -o -c. Decode a complete independent frame so this checks publication and output selection. Explicit -o - alone does not enable raw pass-through under force.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > in.zst
zstd -qdc -o named in.zst
zstd -qd -o unused -c in.zst
[[ -f named && ! -e unused ]]
printf 'raw input\n' > plain
if zstd -qdf -o - plain; then exit 9; else [[ $? == 1 ]]; fi

cases.purpose: Successful named decode preserves source mode/mtime and --rm removes the source only after completion. Check timestamps explicitly because the harness compares bytes, modes and links.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > in.zst
chmod 640 in.zst
/usr/bin/touch -t 202001020304.05 in.zst
zstd -qd --rm in.zst
[[ ! -e in.zst ]]
[[ $(/usr/bin/stat -c %a in) == 640 ]]
[[ $(/usr/bin/stat -c %Y in) == 1577934245 ]]
cat in

cases.purpose: Refuse an existing named target without force; retain both original input and destination.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > in.zst
printf '%b' '\x6f\x6c\x64\x20\x64\x65\x73\x74\x69\x6e\x61\x74\x69\x6f\x6e\x0a' > in
zstd -qd in.zst

cases.purpose: Independent preservation contract: direct source, hardlink source alias and symlink destination must be refused under force, leaving bytes and link topology intact.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > in.zst
ln in.zst alias
ln -s in.zst symlink
for target in in.zst alias symlink; do
 if zstd -qdf -o "$target" in.zst; then exit 9; else [[ $? == 1 ]]; fi
done
[[ in.zst -ef alias && -L symlink ]]
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > expected
/usr/bin/cmp in.zst expected
[[ -z $(compgen -G '*.tmp.*') ]]
printf 'protected\n'

cases.purpose: Independent atomic-publication contract (stronger than CLI parity): a recognized but truncated frame must fail with --rm and force, preserving the previous destination and source and cleaning temporary files.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61' > broken.zst
printf '%b' '\x6f\x72\x69\x67\x69\x6e\x61\x6c\x0a' > destination
printf '%b' '\x6f\x72\x69\x67\x69\x6e\x61\x6c\x0a' > expected
if zstd -qdf --rm -o destination broken.zst; then exit 9; else [[ $? == 1 ]]; fi
[[ -f broken.zst ]]
/usr/bin/cmp destination expected
[[ -z $(compgen -G '*.tmp.*') ]]
printf 'preserved\n'

cases.purpose: Documented override contract: an unavailable relative library fails without affecting the shell; unset and empty overrides use the linked decoder successfully. Fresh process avoids caching a prior library.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > in.zst
export BASHOS_ZSTD_LIB=./missing-libzstd.so
if zstd -dc in.zst; then exit 9; else [[ $? == 1 ]]; fi
unset BASHOS_ZSTD_LIB
zstd -dc in.zst
export BASHOS_ZSTD_LIB=''
zstd -dc in.zst

cases.purpose: Decode supported empty, skippable, unknown-size and ordinary frames in a single bounded stream.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x50\x2a\x4d\x18\x00\x00\x00\x00\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x00\x01\x00\x00\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x00\x00\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > joined.zst
zstd -dc joined.zst

cases.purpose: A missing operand and a recognized incomplete frame both fail; continue to decode the subsequent valid input, returning aggregate failure.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06' > broken.zst
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > good.zst
zstd -dc absent.zst broken.zst good.zst

cases.purpose: Round-trip NUL and 0xff bytes through level 3 stdin/stdout streams, then round-trip an empty stream at level 19. This checks byte preservation and valid empty frames without comparing encoded bytes.
cases.script:
printf '\000A\377\n' | zstd -q -3 -c - | /usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c -
printf '' | zstd -q -19 -c - | /usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c -

cases.purpose: Exercise the documented supported compression endpoints, levels 1 and 19, with named input and stdout output; each generated stream must decode to the original bytes.
cases.script:
printf 'endpoint payload\n' > input
zstd -q -1 -c input | /usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c -
zstd -q -19 -c input | /usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c -

cases.purpose: Decode a static one-byte raw-block Zstandard frame encoded from the published frame format, rather than from either implementation under test. GNU zstd independently validates the frame and both sides must emit exactly A.

Check default named output keeps source. Independently decode each compressed artifact and compare decoded bytes, source effects and target modes. Remove only the verified encoded artifacts because valid encoders may produce different frame bytes; compare the entire remaining tree.
cases.script:
printf 'named payload\n' > data
zstd -q data
[[ -f data && -f data.zst ]] || exit 11
/usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c data.zst
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a" data.zst
rm data.zst

cases.purpose: Check multiple named inputs. Independently decode each compressed artifact and compare decoded bytes, source effects and target modes. Remove only the verified encoded artifacts because valid encoders may produce different frame bytes; compare the entire remaining tree.
cases.script:
printf 'first\n' > first
printf 'second\000record\n' > second
zstd -q first second
[[ -f first && -f first.zst && -f second && -f second.zst ]] || exit 12
/usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c first.zst
/usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c second.zst
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a" first.zst second.zst
rm first.zst second.zst

cases.purpose: Check stdin to named output. Independently decode each compressed artifact and compare decoded bytes, source effects and target modes. Remove only the verified encoded artifacts because valid encoders may produce different frame bytes; compare the entire remaining tree.
cases.script:
printf 'stdin named target\n' | zstd -q -o result.zst -
[[ -f result.zst ]] || exit 13
/usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c result.zst
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a" result.zst
rm result.zst

cases.purpose: Check remove source after success. Independently decode each compressed artifact and compare decoded bytes, source effects and target modes. Remove only the verified encoded artifacts because valid encoders may produce different frame bytes; compare the entire remaining tree.
cases.script:
printf 'remove only after success\n' > cleanup
zstd -q --rm cleanup
[[ ! -e cleanup && -f cleanup.zst ]] || exit 14
/usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c cleanup.zst
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a" cleanup.zst
rm cleanup.zst

cases.purpose: Check no clobber and force. Independently decode each compressed artifact and compare decoded bytes, source effects and target modes. Remove only the verified encoded artifacts because valid encoders may produce different frame bytes; compare the entire remaining tree.
cases.script:
printf 'new contents\n' > source
printf 'keep destination\n' > source.zst
if zstd -q source; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 1 && $(<source.zst) == 'keep destination' ]] || exit 15
printf 'no-clobber preserved\n'
zstd -q -f source
[[ -f source && -f source.zst ]] || exit 16
/usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c source.zst
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a" source.zst
rm source.zst

cases.purpose: Check the documented failure status for bad magic and a missing named input, while ensuring both errors produce no decoded bytes. Diagnostics are compared only as nonempty because wording varies by zstd version.
cases.script:
printf 'not a zstd frame\n' > bad.zst
if zstd -q -d -c bad.zst > bad.out; then badrc=0; else badrc=$?; fi
if zstd -q -d -c absent.zst > absent.out; then missingrc=0; else missingrc=$?; fi
[[ $badrc == 1 && $missingrc == 1 && ! -s bad.out && ! -s absent.out ]] || exit 17
printf 'bad=%d missing=%d\n' "$badrc" "$missingrc"

cases.purpose: Compare --no-content-size acceptance and interoperability on ordinary stdin using the independent installed decoder.
cases.script: printf 'unknown-size payload\n' | zstd -q --no-content-size -c - | /usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c -

cases.purpose: Check builtin registration and availability of the documented compression synopsis; metadata only.
cases.script: type -t zstd; synopsis=$(help -s zstd); [[ $synopsis == zstd:* ]]; printf "help available\n"

cases.purpose: The documented BASHOS_ZSTD_LIB override must fail cleanly if its relative fixture library is absent, leave output empty, and return control to the calling shell. This checks a candidate-specific documented contract, not GNU CLI parity.
cases.script:
printf 'payload' > input
if BASHOS_ZSTD_LIB=./absent-libzstd.so zstd -q -c input > output; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 1 && ! -s output ]] || exit 18
printf 'override=%d shell-continues\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Independently inspect the published frame descriptor to require no content-size field for named and empty inputs, then decode with the installed CLI and compare decoded bytes. Encoded artifacts are removed only after checks.
cases.script:
printf 'named payload\n' > source
zstd -q --no-content-size -o named.zst source
printf '' | zstd -q --no-content-size -c - > empty.zst
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PYCODE'
from pathlib import Path
for name in ('named.zst', 'empty.zst'):
    data = Path(name).read_bytes()
    assert data[:4] == bytes.fromhex('28b52ffd')
    assert data[4] & 0xe0 == 0, 'frame descriptor contains a content-size field'
    print('frame content size absent')
PYCODE
/usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c named.zst > decoded
/usr/bin/zstd -q -d -c empty.zst > decoded-empty
rm named.zst empty.zst
